title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is writing up the theory of the Cartier operator for a morphism of characteristic-p schemes X → S, using the relative Frobenius F_{X/S}: X → X^{p/S} = X ×_{S,F_S} S. Λ (or A) denotes the sheaf of rings O_{X^{p/S}}, viewed inside the d-closed functions on X. C̃ is the Cartier operator on closed 1-forms, and ω̃ is the Frobenius pull-back of ω to X^{p/S} (so ω = Σ c_i dx_i gives ω̃ = Σ c_i^p dx̃_i).

What the previous page sets up: L = O_X carries the connection ∇ = ∇_0 + ω, where ∇_0 = d. Two computations are made there.
- Flatness of ∇ is equivalent to dω = 0.
- Jacobson's formula gives (D_i + c_i)^p = D_i^p + c_i^p + D_i^{p-1} c_i, with D_i^p = 0. So vanishing p-curvature means c_i^p + D_i^{p-1} c_i = 0 for all i.
- Cartier's formula C̃ω = −Σ D_i^{p-1} c_i dx̃_i then shows that this vanishing is exactly C̃ω = ω̃.

This page:
1. Cartier descent says a flat quasi-coherent module with p-curvature zero is the same as a module with descent data from X to X^{p/S}. So L with ∇_0 + ω descends to an invertible L_0 on (X^{p/S}, Λ).
2. Locally L_0 has a basis. Hence L is locally generated by a horizontal section f, i.e. df + fω = 0. Up to sign convention this says ω = df/f.
3. Theorem: a 1-form ω is locally a logarithmic derivative df/f, with f a unit, iff dω = 0 and C̃ω = ω̃.
4. Equivalently, dlog: O_X^* → Ω^1_{X/S} has image the subsheaf {ω : dω = 0, C̃ω = ω̃}. Its kernel is Λ^*, the units of the d-closed functions coming from X^{p/S}. He adds that if S is reduced this kernel is O_X^{*p}.

Start of §6 (smooth case): if X/S is smooth, so is X^{p/S}. Then F_{X/S} is finite locally free, radicial and surjective. This prepares the next page:
- X/S has local p-bases;
- C̃ is defined on F_*(ZΩ^•);
- in top degree n, C̃: F_*ω_{X/S} → ω_{X^{p/S}} equals the trace (duality) map of the finite morphism F_{X/S};
- this is checked through residue symbols res(ω/f_1^p…f_n^p) against res(ϖ/f̃_1…f̃_n).
errors: Kernel claim: ker(dlog) consists of the units of O_X ∩ ker d, which for X smooth over S is the image of O_{X^{p/S}}, i.e. units of O_S·O_X^p. This equals O_X^{*p} when S is perfect, not merely reduced. Counterexample: S = X = Spec k with k imperfect and t ∈ k not a p-th power; then dt/t = 0 in Ω_{X/k} = 0, but t ∉ k^{*p}. So 'S réduit' should read 'S parfait', unless the word on the page is actually 'parfait'.

Sign convention: a horizontal section of d + ω satisfies df = −fω, so ω = −df/f. Either the connection is d − ω or a sign is suppressed. This does not affect the theorem, since −df/f = d(f^{-1})/f^{-1}.
The theorem as stated needs a Cartier-isomorphism / p-basis setting so that C̃ is defined; the needed hypotheses were fixed earlier (local p-basis).

ideas.what: A closed 1-form is locally logarithmic (df/f) iff it is fixed by the Cartier operator; exact description of image and kernel of dlog
ideas.modern_name: Cartier's characterization of logarithmic differentials; exact sequence 0 → O^{*p} → O^* → Ω^1_{log} → 0 with Ω^1_log = ker(1 − C) on closed forms
ideas.usually_credited_to: P. Cartier (1957, 'Une nouvelle opération sur les formes différentielles'; Sém. Chevalley 1958/59); later used by Milne and Illusie (logarithmic de Rham–Witt)
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA as such; possibly in the typescript this file annotates (Gauss–Manin/Cartier notes, [1972]–1981)

ideas.what: Proof via the connection d + ω: flatness ⇔ dω = 0, p-curvature zero ⇔ Cω = ω̃, then Frobenius (Cartier) descent
ideas.modern_name: Cartier descent / Katz's theorem: flat connections with zero p-curvature ⇔ modules on the Frobenius twist; p-curvature of d + ω equals ω^p-type term minus Cω
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cartier; N. Katz (1970, 'Nilpotent connections and the monodromy theorem', §5)

ideas.what: Relative Frobenius F_{X/S} of a smooth morphism is finite locally free, radicial and surjective; local p-bases
Announced: top-degree Cartier operator equals the trace map of the finite flat morphism F_{X/S}
ideas.modern_name: Cartier operator = Grothendieck trace for Frobenius (F_*ω_X → ω_{X'})
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; Hartshorne/Lipman/Kunz residue theory; standard in Frobenius-splitting literature (Mehta–Ramanathan, Brion–Kumar)

deep.surprise_reason: A clean relative-base write-up of Cartier's classical theorem on logarithmic forms, proved via p-curvature and Frobenius descent (the Katz-style argument). It ends with the standard trace interpretation of the top-degree Cartier operator. All of this is well known. The only notable detail is the slightly incorrect kernel statement for non-perfect reduced bases.
transcription_corrections: Section title likely reads 'Relations avec la trace des formes diff. de degré maximum' rather than 'la structure [?] des formes'. This fits Théorème 3 on the next page (Cartier operator = trace).
Kernel is written as an underlined Λ^* (the same sheaf as in X_0^{p/S} = (X^{p/S}, Λ)), not A^*; the macron in 'loc. on a' should be read normally.
'il f. et s. que l'on ait dω = 0, C̃ω = ω̃' — the inserted 'C̃ω = ω̃' sits above the line as an addition, as transcribed.
The word in 'si S est réduit' is hard to read; mathematically 'parfait' would be correct.
